name: Spiked leather helmet
description: An old officer's helmet of hardened black leather with a peak front and back, a tall spike on a cross-shaped base, a shield-shaped plate on the front and scaled chin straps. The spike is for show.
notes: Standing on its rim, front on +z, 232 mm across, 268 mm front to back with the peaks and 244 mm tall to the spike tip: a black leather shell in `leather-black`, a front peak trimmed in metal and a deeper neck peak, a fluted spike on a round boss with four arms down the shell, a shield-shaped front plate, rosettes each side and a run of chin scales resting over the front peak. The fittings are in `brass-polished` because polished fittings are how the helmet is known and steel would not read against the trim at this grain. A helmet is a hollow shell with a spike, so the box round the head it encloses is mostly air. Slot `head`. Protection is a guess for hardened leather. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points at the left side, right side and back of the rim; no front mount, because the front plate takes the brow. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Pot helmet
description: An iron soup pot worn upside down, with a leather strap run through its side handles to buckle under the chin. Poor armour, but it still cooks.
notes: Upside down on its rim, front on +z: an iron pot 200 mm across and 130 mm deep in `iron-cast` with a rolled rim, a loop handle each side near the rim and a brown strap dropping from both handles and lying out in a loop in front with its buckle, 256 mm across with the handles. Slot `head`. Protection is a guess for a thin iron pot. No `helmet` points: a pot has no rails or rim laces to take add-ons. The xs size shares the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Canning pot helmet
description: A huge enamelled canning pot worn upside down, with a strap through its handles. It swallows an ordinary head whole and still cooks.
notes: Upside down on its rim, front on +z: a steel canner 330 mm across and 260 mm deep, enamelled in `paint-drum-blue` with a `steel-grey` rim and handles, and a brown strap through both handles lying out in a loop in front, 384 mm across with the handles. Built by the same pot helper as `pot_helmet`, larger and in another finish. The name says which pot it is. Slot `head`. Protection is a guess for thicker steel than the soup pot. No `helmet` points: a pot has no rails or rim laces to take add-ons. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Stock pot great helm
description: A tall aluminium stock pot turned upside down into a closed helm, with a T hacked through the front to see and breathe, a blanket stuffed inside for padding and cords tied to the handles to hold it on. Hot, stifling and hard to see out of.
notes: Upside down on its rim, front on +z: an aluminium stock pot 260 mm across and 290 mm deep in `alu-bare`, a T cut through the front wall with the dark blanket showing through it, a grey blanket bunched out under the rim all round, and a cotton cord tied to each side handle hanging to the floor and trailing forward, 328 mm across with the cords. Slot `head`; it also covers the eyes and mouth, which the head slot is taken to include. Protection is a guess for an aluminium pot over a blanket. No `helmet` points: a pot has no rails or rim laces to take add-ons. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Tactical full helmet
description: A charcoal-grey ballistic helmet that closes over the whole head and neck, with a moulded chin bar, a smoked visor curving round the face, black accessory rails along the sides and a mount over the brow.
notes: Standing on its neck guard, front on +z, 272 mm across and 304 mm tall: a rounded shell in `plastic-charcoal` with a chin bar and a row of black vents, a smoked visor in `lens-smoke` curving close round the shell to its pivots, with a black rim across its top, visor pivots each side, accessory rails curved along the sides behind the pivots, trim in `plastic-matte-black`, a mount shroud above the brow and a guard flaring out over the back of the neck. Tiles draw the visor opaque; it stays see-through in the game. A helmet is a hollow shell, so the box round the head it encloses is mostly air. Slot `head`; it also covers the eyes and mouth, which the head slot is taken to include. Protection is a guess for rigid aramid with a plastic visor. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points on the left and right rails and at the back of the shell, and the shroud above the brow as the front mount for goggles. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
